title: Transient Behavior of Threshold-Dependent Ruin and Queueing Models with Phase-Type Jumps
summary: We study the transient behavior of two threshold-dependent stochastic models: a Cramér--Lundberg risk model and an M/G/1-type queueing model. In both models, the dynamics are driven by two different compound Poisson processes with drift, with the governing process depending on whether the current state is below or above a fixed threshold. For the risk model, we characterize the probability of ruin before an exponentially distributed epoch, while for the queueing model, we characterize the Laplace--Stieltjes transform of the workload at an exponentially distributed epoch.
